key_insight: This paper provides a unified empirical comparison of quantum machine learning and classical machine learning models, aiming to clarify whether QML actually performs better in practice. The main takeaway is that quantum advantages should be evaluated carefully and empirically rather than assumed.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of solid evidence about whether quantum ML models outperform classical counterparts, and it standardizes comparisons across different model families to make results more reliable.
method: Compare seven pairs of quantum and classical models across supervised and/or related learning tasks.
Use a unified empirical evaluation framework so performance differences are measured consistently.
Analyze model behavior and results to identify where QML helps, matches, or falls behind classical methods.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this helps separate hype from evidence and provides a clearer basis for deciding when quantum methods are worth exploring. It also offers a benchmark-style view that can guide future hybrid and quantum-ready ML research.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison table of quantum vs. classical model pairs
Performance bar charts showing accuracy or loss across tasks
Pipeline diagram of the unified evaluation framework
Icon set contrasting quantum circuit symbols with classical neural network blocks
paper_title: Quantum vs. Classical Machine Learning: A Unified Empirical Comparison
paper_authors: Chuanming Yu, Jiaming Liu, Zihao Ge, Xiongfei Wu, Lulu Zhu
